post.description:
Send a set of commands to one or more vehicles using a predefined model.
Models group multiple templates into a single execution flow.

**Use cases:**
- Execute multiple related commands in sequence
- Configure vehicles with predefined settings
- Automate complex command workflows

**Important notes:**
- Model must be active and visible to the user
- Vehicle must be active and have a linked device
- All templates in the model are executed in order
- Parameters are applied to matching templates only
- Optional templates are executed even without parameters
- Commands are queued and processed asynchronously

**Execution flow:**
1. Model templates are sorted by their index
2. Parameters are matched to templates by template ID
3. Each template is executed in order
4. Optional templates use default parameter values
5. A single request history tracks all commands

modelWithParams.description: Execute model with custom parameters for specific templates

simpleModel.description: Execute all templates with default values

modelId.description: Unique identifier of the model to execute

modulo.description: Module or feature name requesting the command

params.description:
List of parameters for specific templates in the model.
Each parameter group must specify the template ID.
Templates without parameters will use default values.

paramName.description: Name of the parameter as defined in the template

paramValue.description: Value to replace the parameter with

templateId.description: ID of the template to apply parameters to

phoneNumber.description:
Phone number for SMS delivery (required only for SMS send type).
Must be in E.164 format (e.g., +5511999999999)

smsProvider.description: SMS provider to use (only applicable for SMS send type)

vehicleId.description: Unique identifier of the target vehicle

requestHistoryId.description: Unique identifier for tracking all commands in the model

400.description:
Bad request - possible causes:
- Missing required fields
- Invalid parameter values
- Template parameters mismatch
- Invalid phone number format
- Template not found in model

403.description:
Forbidden - possible causes:
- Model not visible to user
- Vehicle does not belong to user's central
- Insufficient permissions

404.description:
Not found - possible causes:
- Model does not exist
- Vehicle does not exist
- Vehicle has no linked device
- One or more templates in the model do not exist

422.description:
Unprocessable entity - possible causes:
- Vehicle is inactive
- Device is not communicating
- Model is inactive
- One or more templates in the model are inactive

x-codeSamples.label: Execute simple model
x-codeSamples.source:
curl -X POST 'https://api.getrak.com/v1.0/commands/models/commands' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_TOKEN>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "modelId": 6,
    "vehicleId": 54321,
    "modulo": "comando"
  }'

put.description:
Cancels a batch of commands sent via template. This operation updates the command status to 'C' (Canceled) and removes them from the Redis queue.

Only commands with status 'P' (Pending) or 'N' (Not Processed) can be canceled.

**Requirements:**
- Template must have sendType `gateway` or `gateway_legacy`
- Commands must exist and not be processed yet
- Command IDs must be valid positive integers

**Response includes:**
- Total number of commands in the batch
- Number of successful cancellations
- Number of failed cancellations
- List of successful command IDs
- List of errors with command ID and error message
- Overall result: `success`, `error`, or `partial`

post.description:
Creates a new geofence (cerca). Supports four creation modes via `type`:

- **polygon** (default): provide `shape` with polygon coordinates (min 4 points per ring).
- **circle**: provide `coordinates` (center) and `radius` (meters). Converted to polygon server-side via @turf/circle.
- **distance**: provide `coordinates` (center) and `range_value` (meters). Polygon generated via HERE Isoline API (distance-based).
- **time**: provide `coordinates` (center) and `range_value` (seconds). Polygon generated via HERE Isoline API (time-based).

**Role-based access:**
- ADMIN / OPERADOR: can optionally assign to any client via `client_id` in body
- CLIENTE / SUBCLIENTE: `client_id` is ignored, automatically linked to their own company (from token)

For polygon type, if the last point differs from the first, the polygon is auto-closed.
Name must be unique within the central.

category_custom_fields.description: Custom field values for the category (optional). Stored as JSON in `categoria_item.valores_adicionais`.

tipo.description: Field type: text, data, hora, datahora, numero, selecao, icone

category_id.description: Category ID to link (optional). References `categoria` table.

client_id.description: Client ID to associate. Only used by ADMIN/OPERADOR roles; ignored for other roles.

radius.description: Radius in meters (required for type `circle`, min 50)

range_value.description: Range value for isoline (required for types `distance` and `time`). Meters for distance, seconds for time.

shape.description: Polygon rings (required for type `polygon`). Min 1 ring, min 4 points per ring including closing.

type.description:
Geofence creation mode. Default: `polygon`.
- `polygon`: requires `shape`
- `circle`: requires `coordinates` and `radius`
- `distance`: requires `coordinates` and `range_value` (meters)
- `time`: requires `coordinates` and `range_value` (seconds)

x-codeSamples.source:
curl -X POST 'https://api.getrak.com/v1.0/perimeters/geofences' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_TOKEN>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"Cerca Centro","shape":[[{"x":-46.5,"y":-23.4},{"x":-46.6,"y":-23.5},{"x":-46.4,"y":-23.3},{"x":-46.5,"y":-23.4}]]}'

post.description:
Create a new telemetry configuration (alert template). A telemetry is NOT immediately linked to vehicles - it creates a template that can be applied later.

**Structure:**
- 1 telemetry = 1-4 verifications (conditions)
- Telemetries created here are templates stored in the central's catalog
- To apply to vehicles: use POST /vehicles/{id}/default-telemetries or vehicle binding endpoints

**Business Rules:**
- Maximum 4 verifications per telemetry
- Verification type 30 (no_communication_time) can only be used with verification 1
- Name must be unique within the central
- `days` uses bit flags: 1=Sun, 2=Mon, 4=Tue, 8=Wed, 16=Thu, 32=Fri, 64=Sat (127=all days)

accumulation_mode.description:
Accumulation mode for multiple occurrences:
- 0: Accumulate all (default)
- 1: Accumulate while same verification
- 2: Accumulate and close on different verification

contact_phones.description: Phone numbers for SMS notifications (legacy compatibility)

days.description:
Days of week as bit flags (1=Sun, 2=Mon, 4=Tue, 8=Wed, 16=Thu, 32=Fri, 64=Sat)
Examples: 127=all days, 62=Mon-Fri, 65=Sun+Sat

name.description: Telemetry name (must be unique within central)

notification_channels.description:
Notification channels as bit flags:
- 1: SMS
- 2: Email
- 4: GConnect App
Example: 7 = all channels (1+2+4)

parameter.description:
Parameter value - format depends on verification type:
- For selects/multiselects: IDs separated by pipe (e.g., "10|15|20")
- For text inputs: text value (e.g., "30" for 30 minutes)
- For none: empty string ""

post.description:
Reactivate (end) the suspension of multiple vehicles for a given telemetry at once.

For each vehicle ID provided, the service validates that the vehicle is bound
to the telemetry within the authenticated user's central and has an active suspension.

**Validations:**
- The telemetry must belong to the user's central (validated via `central` query param)
- Each vehicle must have an active bind to the telemetry
- Vehicles without an active suspension are skipped
- Client-level access control is enforced when the user has a `client_id`

post.description:
Sends batch commands to multiple vehicles/modules using a pre-registered template.

## Authentication & Authorization

- **Supported authorities**: `GetrakWeb`, `GetrakChatbot`, `GetrakPed`, `Integracao` (client_credentials), `Integrador`

## Payload Structure by SendType

The vehicle object structure varies based on the template's `sendType`:

### Gateway / Gateway Legacy
```json
{
  "templateId": 1,
  "vehicles": [
    { "vehicleId": 123 }
  ]
}
```
- **Returns**: `commandId` in response (command stored in Redis and database)

### Gateway GTM
```json
{
  "templateId": 1,
  "vehicles": [
    { "vehicleId": 123 }
  ]
}
```
- **Returns**: `requestHistoryId` in response (request-history created for tracking)

### SMS
```json
{
  "templateId": 1,
  "vehicles": [
    { "vehicleId": 123, "phoneNumber": "82993427289" }
  ]
}
```
- **Required**: `phoneNumber` for each vehicle
- **Optional**: `smsProvider` (default provider used if not specified)
- **Returns**: `requestHistoryId` in response

## Response Structure

Each vehicle in the response includes:
- `vehicleId`: Vehicle ID (if provided in request)
- `modulo`: Module/device identifier
- `status`: "success" or "error"
- `commandId`: Database command ID (only for Gateway/GatewayLegacy on success)
- `requestHistoryId`: Request history ID (only for GatewayGTM/SMS on success)
- `error`: Error message (only on failure)

### Possible error messages:
- "User does not have access to this vehicle" - User doesn't own the vehicle (GetrakWeb only)
- "Vehicle does not have associated equipment" - Vehicle has no device assigned
- "Command queue already contains commands" - Vehicle has pending commands (only for Gateway/GatewayLegacy)
- "Failed to validate vehicle access" - Error during access validation
- "Access denied" - Generic access error

# Webhook Integration

The Getrak telemetry platform exposes a real-time data stream of normalized telematic packets, delivered to
integrators as they arrive from tracking devices. This guide covers the full architecture, routing logic,
message format, and best practices for consuming this stream reliably.

You choose how each destination receives the packets:

| Protocol | How you receive | Who creates the destination |
|---|---|---|
| **`amqp`** | Getrak publishes each packet to your private RabbitMQ queue. You consume it. | Getrak, on request |
| **`http`** | Getrak sends each packet to your endpoint with a POST request. | You, through the [Webhooks API](#tag/WebhooksIntegracao) |

The packet payload is identical for both protocols. Only the transport changes, so you can move from one to the
other without changing how you read the data.

---

## Architecture Overview

The data pipeline flows through five distinct stages before a packet reaches an integrator queue:

<details>
<summary>Show diagram</summary>

![RabbitMQ Integration Architecture](https://assets.getrak.com.br/apidoc/Webhook.png)

</details>

### Stage descriptions

| Stage | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| **Tracking Devices** | Send raw telematic frames over TCP, UDP, HTTP, or proprietary protocols |
| **Gateways** | Decode device-specific frames and produce the unified internal JSON format |
| **Processing Queue** | Internal buffer that decouples gateway throughput from core persistence |
| **Getrak Platform** | Persists the packet to the primary database, then publishes the normalized packet to the Router |
| **Router** | Looks up which destinations are subscribed to the vehicle, then delivers the packet to each one through its own protocol |
| **Destinations** | Your private RabbitMQ queue, your HTTP endpoint, or both — no cross-integrator visibility |

---

## Getting Access

Each integrator receives the following **via e-mail**:

| Item | Description |
|---|---|
| **Integration ID** | Unique identifier used to associate vehicles with this integrator via the Webhook API |
| **Queue URI** | Full AMQP(S) connection string, including hostname, vhost, username, and password. Only for `amqp` destinations |
| **Credentials** | Embedded in the queue URI — handle with the same care as a password |

Use the **Integration ID** together with the [Webhooks API](#tag/WebhooksIntegracao) endpoints to register the
vehicles whose packets you want to receive.

To receive packets over HTTP, create the destination yourself with `POST /v1.0/webhooks/config`. You do not
need to contact Getrak.

---

## Routing Logic

The Router processes every normalized packet published by the Getrak Platform:

1. **Identify the vehicle** — resolved from the `mod` field (device serial with manufacturer prefix).
2. **Look up subscriptions** — query which destinations have registered interest in that vehicle.
3. **Fan out** — deliver a copy of the packet to each matching destination, through the protocol that destination declares.

If no destination has subscribed to a given vehicle, the packet is simply not forwarded — there is no overhead
on the integrator side.

A vehicle can have more than one destination. Each destination receives its own copy, so you can run an `amqp`
destination and an `http` destination in parallel while you migrate from one to the other.

> The JSON payload is **already normalized**, and it is byte for byte the same under both protocols. No further
> transformation by the gateway or router layer is required on the consumer side.

---

## HTTP Delivery Rules

These rules apply to destinations with `protocol: http`.

| Rule | Value / Detail |
|---|---|
| **Method** | `POST`, and only `POST` |
| **Content type** | `application/json` |
| **Body** | One packet per request, in the same format delivered to a queue |
| **Authentication** | Your API key in the `x-api-key` header |
| **Success** | Any `2xx` status |
| **Timeout** | **2 seconds** — answer fast, then process asynchronously on your side |
| **Retry** | None. A failed delivery is logged and the packet is dropped |
| **Redirects** | Not followed. A `3xx` response counts as a failed delivery |

Two consequences deserve attention when you build the receiving endpoint.

First, **acknowledge before you process**. The 2 second timeout covers the whole request. Persist the packet or
enqueue it internally, answer `2xx`, and do the heavy work after. An endpoint that validates, enriches, and
writes to a slow database inside the request will start losing packets under load.

Second, **there is no retry**. If your endpoint is unreachable or answers an error, that packet is lost. Design
for continuous availability, and prefer an `amqp` destination if you need the platform to hold packets while
your consumer is down.

Rotating your API key takes effect within **2 hours**, because the routing service caches the destination
configuration. Keep the previous key valid during that window.

---

## Queue Rules

These rules apply to destinations with `protocol: amqp`.

| Rule | Value / Detail |
|---|---|
| **Message TTL** | **12 hours** — unread messages are automatically discarded after this period |
| **Queue isolation** | Each integrator has a dedicated private queue; no cross-integrator visibility |
| **Delivery guarantee** | At-least-once — always send explicit **ACK** after processing to prevent redelivery |
| **Pricing** | Not yet finalized — integrators will be notified officially when pricing is available |

The 12-hour TTL is intentional: it prevents unbounded queue growth, reduces storage costs, and keeps the
stream relevant. Design your consumer to operate continuously rather than in large batch windows.

---

## Packet Data Fields

All fields are **optional** — different device models emit different subsets. Always treat each field as
nullable: `"field": <value | null>`.

> For a precise, per-model breakdown of exactly which fields are emitted, their Go types, presence rules,
> and packet-type-level details, see the [Device Field Reference](#tag/RabbitMQDeviceFields).

### 1. GPS & Location

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `dt` | `string (date-time)[]` | Timestamp(s) from the device clock |
| `dataServidor` | `string (date-time)` | Server timestamp — when the packet was received by the platform |
| `fix` | `boolean` | `true` if the GPS position is valid |
| `lat` | `number` | Latitude (decimal degrees) |
| `lon` | `number` | Longitude (decimal degrees) |
| `alt` | `number` | Altitude (metres) |
| `velocidade` | `number` | Speed (km/h) |
| `dir` | `integer` | Heading / course, `0–359°` |
| `hod` | `number` | Odometer reading |
| `ns` | `integer` | Number of GPS satellites in use |
| `hor` | `number` | Hour-meter (engine operating hours) |

### 2. Inputs, Outputs & Vehicle State

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `i` | `boolean` | Ignition — `true` = on |
| `ali` | `number` | External power / main battery voltage |
| `p` | `boolean` | Panic button state |
| `ef` | `integer[]` | Digital inputs / sensor readings |
| `s` | `integer[]` | Digital outputs / actuator states |
| `evid` | `integer` | Active event / status code |

### 3. Energy & Batteries

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `bat` | `number` | External (main) battery voltage (V) |
| `batb` | `number` | Internal / backup battery voltage (V) |
| `pb` | `number` | Battery charge percentage (0–100) |

### 4. Additional Sensors

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `tmp` | `number` | Temperature (°C) |
| `fl` | `number` | Fuel level |

### 5. Cellular Network & LBS

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `gsms` / `sgsm` | `integer` | GSM signal strength (dBm or manufacturer scale) |
| `mcc` | `integer` | Mobile Country Code |
| `mnc` | `integer` | Mobile Network Code |
| `cellid` | `integer` | Cell tower ID |
| `lac` | `integer` | Location Area Code (LAC) |
| `lbs` | `integer` | LBS mode presence / signal strength |

### 6. Identification & Control

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `seq` | `integer` | Position sequence number / packet counter |
| `mod` | `string` | Device serial — `{PREFIX}{IMEI}`, e.g. `"YZ865267081426614"` |
| `ev` | `integer` | Primary event code |
| `evs` | `integer` | Sub-event code |
| `rpt` | `string` | Report type |
| `ver` | `string` | Protocol / firmware version |
| `rt` | `integer` | `1` = real-time packet, `0` = buffered / accumulated packet |
| `mt` | `integer` | Thread / channel identifier |
| `mot` | `string` | Driver ID (iButton, RFID, etc.) |

### 7. Alarms

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `alarmid` | `integer` | Alarm code reported by the device module |

---

## Device Prefixes

The `mod` field encodes the manufacturer and model as a 2-character prefix preceding the device serial number
(IMEI or proprietary serial). The Router uses this prefix for fast device-type identification.

**Example:**
```json
{ "mod": "YZ865267081426614" }
```

## Consumer Examples

### Node.js (Express) — receiving an `http` destination

```javascript
const express = require('express');

const app = express();
app.use(express.json());

const API_KEY = process.env.WEBHOOK_API_KEY;

app.post('/pacotes', (req, res) => {
  if (req.get('x-api-key') !== API_KEY) {
    return res.sendStatus(401);
  }

  // Answer first. The delivery times out after 2 seconds and is never retried.
  res.sendStatus(204);

  // Then process out of the request path.
  enqueueForProcessing(req.body);
});

app.listen(3000);
```

### Node.js (amqplib) — consuming an `amqp` destination

```javascript
const amqp = require('amqplib');

const QUEUE_URI = process.env.RABBITMQ_URI; // e.g. amqps://user:pass@host/vhost
const QUEUE_NAME = process.env.RABBITMQ_QUEUE;

async function startConsumer() {
  let connection;

  try {
    connection = await amqp.connect(QUEUE_URI);
    const channel = await connection.createChannel();

    // Ensure at-most-one unacknowledged message per consumer
    await channel.prefetch(1);

    console.log(`Waiting for messages on queue: ${QUEUE_NAME}`);

    channel.consume(QUEUE_NAME, async (msg) => {
      if (!msg) return;

      try {
        const packet = JSON.parse(msg.content.toString());

        // All fields are optional — handle nulls defensively
        const { mod, lat, lon, velocidade, i, dt } = packet;
        console.log(`[${mod}] lat=${lat ?? 'n/a'} lon=${lon ?? 'n/a'} speed=${velocidade ?? 0} km/h`);

        // Process packet ...

        // Always ACK after successful processing
        channel.ack(msg);
      } catch (err) {
        console.error('Processing error — rejecting without requeue:', err);
        channel.nack(msg, false, false);
      }
    });
  } catch (err) {
    console.error('Connection error:', err);
    setTimeout(startConsumer, 5000); // simple exponential back-off recommended
  }
}

startConsumer();
```

### Python (pika)

```python
import os
import json
import time
import pika

QUEUE_URI = os.environ['RABBITMQ_URI']
QUEUE_NAME = os.environ['RABBITMQ_QUEUE']

def process(packet: dict) -> None:
    mod = packet.get('mod')
    lat = packet.get('lat')
    lon = packet.get('lon')
    speed = packet.get('velocidade', 0)
    print(f"[{mod}] lat={lat} lon={lon} speed={speed} km/h")
    # Insert your business logic here

def callback(ch, method, properties, body):
    try:
        packet = json.loads(body)
        process(packet)
        ch.basic_ack(delivery_tag=method.delivery_tag)
    except Exception as exc:
        print(f"Processing error: {exc}")
        ch.basic_nack(delivery_tag=method.delivery_tag, requeue=False)

def start():
    params = pika.URLParameters(QUEUE_URI)
    params.heartbeat = 60
    params.blocked_connection_timeout = 300

    connection = pika.BlockingConnection(params)
    channel = connection.channel()
    channel.basic_qos(prefetch_count=1)
    channel.basic_consume(queue=QUEUE_NAME, on_message_callback=callback)

    print(f"Consuming from {QUEUE_NAME} ...")
    channel.start_consuming()

while True:
    try:
        start()
    except Exception as exc:
        print(f"Connection lost: {exc} — retrying in 5 s")
        time.sleep(5)
```

---

## Best Practices

### 1. Consume in real time

For `amqp` destinations, use **continuous workers** (push-based consumers) connected to the queue. Avoid manual
polling — the 12-hour TTL means messages expire whether or not you pull them.

For `http` destinations there is nothing to poll. Keep the endpoint available, because a delivery that fails
is not sent again.

### 2. Always ACK explicitly

For `amqp` destinations, send a positive `ACK` after each successfully processed message. Without an ACK the
broker will redeliver the message to the next available consumer, potentially causing duplicate processing.

For `http` destinations, the `2xx` status is the acknowledgement. Send it before you process the packet, not
after, so that slow processing never causes a timeout.

### 3. Treat the JSON payload as immutable

The packet format is fixed and normalized. If your pipeline requires a different shape, transform a copy
internally — never mutate the original object.

### 4. Implement local retry queues

If your downstream system is temporarily unavailable, buffer failed messages in an internal dead-letter queue
or retry store. Do not rely on RabbitMQ requeue for application-level errors, and never rely on Getrak resending
an `http` delivery — there is no retry on that path.

### 5. Treat all fields as optional / nullable

Different device models report different field sets. Always guard against `null` or absent fields:

```json
{
  "lat": null,
  "lon": null,
  "velocidade": null
}
```

### 6. Log responsibly

Avoid writing full GPS coordinates or personal identifiers (driver ID, plate) to long-lived log files.
Use log rotation with short retention periods and redact sensitive fields where regulations apply.

### 7. Keep your credentials secret

The queue URI contains embedded credentials, and the `http` destination API key authenticates every delivery.
Store both exclusively in environment variables, a secrets manager (AWS Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault, etc.),
or an equivalent secure store. **Never commit them to version control.**

Serve your `http` endpoint over HTTPS. The API key travels in a request header, so plain HTTP exposes it in transit.

### 8. Scale with fleet size

RabbitMQ supports parallel consumers on the same queue. If message throughput grows as your monitored fleet
expands, add workers proportionally.

An `http` endpoint receives one request per packet. Size it for your peak packet rate, and keep the response
well under the 2 second timeout.

### 9. Use auto-reconnect libraries

Network interruptions will occur. Choose a client library that handles reconnection automatically (e.g.,
`amqplib-as-promised` with retry wrappers, Pika's reconnection loop, or Spring AMQP's built-in retry
policy). Your consumer should recover without human intervention.

# Device Field Reference Detailed field-level reference for each supported device model, documenting every JSON field that may appear in a RabbitMQ packet — data types, presence rules, packet types, and sample payloads. > All fields are nullable. Fields marked as _conditional_ are omitted from the JSON payload when their > value is zero. See [Webhook Integration](#tag/RabbitMQIntegration) for the full protocol overview. Expand a model below to view its full reference. --- ## Getrak
GTag  ·  prefix JY  ·  Bluetooth asset tracker The GTag communicates position, battery and cellular data over several distinct packet types. The gateway maps each packet type to the event field `ev`. ### Packet Types | `ev` (decimal) | `ev` (hex) | Packet name | Description | |---|---|---|---| | `18` | `0x12` | Location basic | GPS position + state carried from last heartbeat session | | `23` | `0x17` | Location extended | GPS position + ignition + battery + odometer | | `34` | `0x22` | Location + odometer | GPS position + ignition + odometer + sub-event | | `22` | `0x16` | Alarm | Alarm event with LBS cellular data | | `38` | `0x26` | Alarm extended | Alarm event with extended battery percentage | | `26` | `0x1A` | Address | GPS position from address-type packet | | `21` | `0x15` | Command ACK | Response to a server-initiated position request (`reqpos`) | ### Sub-event Values (`evs`) Only meaningful on alarm packets (`ev` = `22` or `38`). Always `0` on other packet types. | `evs` | Meaning | Side effect | |---|---|---| | `1` | SOS / Panic button | `p` → `1` | | `2` | Power cut / External power removed | `ali` → `0` | ### Field Reference **Presence** legend: **Always** — always present even when `0`. **Conditional** — omitted when zero (`omitempty`). **Session** — carried from last heartbeat; GTK OBD  ·  prefix IS  ·  OBD-II plug-in tracker (4G LTE) The GTK OBD shares the same communication protocol and gateway parser as the GTK ON 4G. The only difference is the physical form factor (OBD-II plug) and the device prefix (`IS` instead of `JH`). All packet types, field semantics, sub-event codes, presence rules, and sample payloads documented for the GTK ON 4G apply identically to the GTK OBD. | Property | Value | |---|---| | **Prefix** | `IS` | | **Protocol** | Identical to GTK ON 4G (`JH`) | | **Packet types** | `0x12`, `0x17`, `0x16`, `0x1A`, `0x94`, `0x15` | The only difference in the payload is the `mod` field prefix: ```json { "mod": "IS0102030405060708" } ``` Refer to the **GTK ON 4G** section above for the complete field reference.

Sample payloads **Location with driver ID** (`ev` = 18): ```json { "mod": "JX0102030405060708", "ev": 18, "evs": 0, "dt": "2026-06-08T14:30:00.512Z", "dataServidor": "2026-06-08T14:30:00.789Z", "fix": 1, "lat": -23.550652, "lon": -46.633308, "velocidade": 62.0, "dir": 180, "ns": 10, "rt": 1, "seq": 512, "mt": 1, "ali": 1, "i": 1, "chrg": 0, "ef": 0, "s": 0, "p": 0, "gsms": 22, "bat": 13.10, "batb": 4.05, "pb": 88, "hod": 72500.0, "hor": "01:45:00", "mot": "a1b2c3d4e5f60708", "fwv": "2.1", "ptv": "1.0", "mcc": 724, "mnc": 5, "lac": 1234, "cellid": 56789 } ``` **BLE uplink** (`ev` = 158): ```json { "mod": "JX0102030405060708", "ev": 158, "evs": 0, "dt": "2026-06-08T14:31:00.000Z", "dataServidor": "2026-06-08T14:31:00.100Z", "mt": 1, "ali": 1, "i": 0, "chrg": 0, "ef": 0, "s": 0, "p": 0, "gsms": 0, "bat": 0.0, "seq": 513, "fwv": "2.1", "ptv": "1.0", "blev": 1, "bledt": 2, "bleid": "AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF", "blers": -72, "blepld": "0201060303AAFE" } ```
---
GTK110 NR01  ·  prefix WW  ·  Vehicle tracker (2G/4G) The NR01 uses a proprietary binary protocol distinct from the other Getrak devices. It defines two message types: a compact position packet and an extended position packet with optional typed extension blocks. Reports **RSSI** (dBm) instead of GSM signal scale, and uses **HDOP** as GPS quality indicator. ### Packet Types | `ev` (decimal) | `ev` (hex) | Packet name | Description | |---|---|---|---| | `16` | `0x10` | Position | Compact GPS + I/O | | `17` | `0x11` | Position extended | Position + optional extension blocks | ### Extension Blocks (ev = 17 only) | Block ID | Name | Fields populated | |---|---|---| | `0x01` | LTE/GPRS | `mcc`, `mnc`, `lac`, `cellid`, `rssi` | | `0x02` | Accelerometer | `acv` (`x`, `y`, `z`) | | `0x03` | Counters | `hod`, `hor` | | `0x04` | Analog input | `ai` | | `0x05` | External tension | `bat` | | `0x06` | Clock | `dt` (fallback) | | `0x07` | ICCID | `iccid` | | `0x08` | Battery | `batb`, `pb` | | `0x0A` | Connection type | `tcon` | | `0x0B` | Altitude | `alt` | | `0x0C` | Temperature | `tmp` | ### Field Reference | Field | JSON key | Go type | Presence | Packet types | Description / Notes | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | Device serial | `mod` | `string` | Always | All | `WW` + zero-padded 15-digit IMEI | | Event ID | `ev` | `uint8` | Always | All | `16` (position) or `17` (extended) | | GPS datetime | `dt` | `string` (ISO 8601) | Always | All | Unix timestamp, UTC; from clock block if GPS has no fix | | Server datetime | `dataServidor` | `string` (ISO 8601 ms) | Always | All | Server receive time, UTC | | GPS fix | `fix` | `uint8` | Always | All | `1` = valid GPS fix | | Latitude | `lat` | `float64` | Always | All | Decimal degrees; negative = South | | Longitude | `lon` | `float64` | Always | All | Decimal degrees; negative = West | | Speed | `velocidade` | `float32` | Always | All | km/h | | Heading | `dir` | `uint16` | Always | All | Course in degrees, `0–359` | | HDOP | `hdop` | `uint8` | Always | All | Horizontal Dilution of Precision | | Satellite count | `ns` | `uint8` | Always | All | GPS satellites used in fix | | External power | `ali` | `uint8` | Always | All | `1` = present; `0` on power-cut event | | Ignition | `i` | `uint8` | Always | All | `1` = on · `0` = off (bit 0 of I/O byte) | | Digital inputs | `ef` | `uint8` | Always | All | Bits 1–4 of I/O byte (4 inputs) | | Digital outputs | `s` | `uint8` | Always | All | Bits 5–7 of I/O byte (3 outputs) | | Thread/channel | `mt` | `uint8` | Always | All | Always `1` | | Mobile Country Code | `mcc` | `uint16` | Extended `0x01` | `0x11` | ITU MCC; omitted when `0` | | Mobile Network Code | `mnc` | `uint16` | Extended `0x01` | `0x11` | ITU MNC; omitted when `0` | | Location Area Code | `lac` | `uint16` | Extended `0x01` | `0x11` | GSM LAC; omitted when `0` | | Cell tower ID | `cellid` | `uint16` | Extended `0x01` | `0x11` | GSM cell tower ID; omitted when `0` | | RSSI | `rssi` | `int8` | Extended `0x01` | `0x11` | Signal strength dBm (signed) | | Accelerometer | `acv` | `object` | Extended `0x02` | `0x11` | Object `{ x, y, z }` (float32 each) | | Odometer | `hod` | `float64` | Extended `0x03` | `0x11` | Distance in km | | Hourmeter | `hor` | `string` | Extended `0x03` | `0x11` | `HH:MM:SS` | | Analog input | `ai` | `float32` | Extended `0x04` | `0x11` | Voltage (V), raw × 0.001 | | External battery voltage | `bat` | `float32` | Extended `0x05` | `0x11` | Main battery (V), raw × 0.001 | | ICCID | `iccid` | `string` | Extended `0x07` | `0x11` | SIM ICCID | | Internal battery voltage | `batb` | `float32` | Extended `0x08` | `0x11` | Backup battery (V), raw × 0.1 | | Battery level | `pb` | `uint8` | Extended `0x08` | `0x11` | Battery % (0–100) | | Connection type | `tcon` | `string` | Extended `0x0A` | `0x11` | `"0"` = 2G, `"1"` = LTE | | Altitude | `alt` | `uint16` | Extended `0x0B` | `0x11` | Altitude in metres | | Temperature | `tmp` | `float32` | Extended `0x0C` | `0x11` | Temperature in °C | **Fields never emitted:** `evs`, `p`, `rt`, `seq`, `gsms`, `lbs`, `mot`, `vex`, `tow`, `fwv`.
Sample payloads **Position** (`ev` = 16): ```json { "mod": "WW000865267081426614", "ev": 16, "dt": "2026-06-08T14:30:00Z", "dataServidor": "2026-06-08T14:30:00.123Z", "fix": 1, "lat": -23.550652, "lon": -46.633308, "velocidade": 45.0, "dir": 180, "hdop": 12, "ns": 9, "ali": 1, "i": 1, "ef": 2, "s": 0, "mt": 1 } ``` **Extended position** (`ev` = 17, all blocks): ```json { "mod": "WW000865267081426614", "ev": 17, "dt": "2026-06-08T14:30:00Z", "dataServidor": "2026-06-08T14:30:00.456Z", "fix": 1, "lat": -23.550652, "lon": -46.633308, "velocidade": 60.0, "dir": 90, "hdop": 8, "ns": 11, "ali": 1, "i": 1, "ef": 0, "s": 0, "mt": 1, "mcc": 724, "mnc": 5, "lac": 1234, "cellid": 5678, "rssi": -85, "acv": { "x": 0.05, "y": -0.02, "z": 9.79 }, "hod": 102300.0, "hor": "03:22:10", "ai": 0.512, "bat": 13.21, "iccid": "89551012341234567890", "batb": 4.1, "pb": 92, "tcon": "1", "alt": 760, "tmp": 24.0 } ```
---
SE 4G PRO  ·  prefix IH  ·  Vehicle tracker (4G LTE) The SE 4G PRO (NR02) shares the same binary protocol as the GTK110 NR01 and adds three extension blocks: driver identification, electronic perimeter events, and raw telemetry package passthrough. All base fields from the GTK110 NR01 apply unchanged. Only additional fields are listed below. ### Additional Extension Blocks | Block ID | Name | Fields populated | |---|---|---| | `0x0D` | Driver | `mot` | | `0x0E` | Electronic perimeter | `efence` | | `0x0F` | Package telemetry | `qi1xx` | ### Additional Fields | Field | JSON key | Go type | Presence | Description | |---|---|---|---|---| | Driver ID | `mot` | `string` | Extended `0x0D` | iButton (hex), RFID or Bluetooth MAC | | Electronic perimeter | `efence` | `int` | Extended `0x0E` | Geofence event code; omitted when `0` | | Package telemetry | `qi1xx` | `string` | Extended `0x0F` | Raw QI-1xx telemetry package (hex) |
Sample payload **Extended position** (`ev` = 17, with driver ID and perimeter): ```json { "mod": "IH000865267081426614", "ev": 17, "dt": "2026-06-08T14:30:00Z", "dataServidor": "2026-06-08T14:30:00.456Z", "fix": 1, "lat": -23.550652, "lon": -46.633308, "velocidade": 48.0, "dir": 270, "hdop": 10, "ns": 9, "ali": 1, "i": 1, "ef": 0, "s": 0, "mt": 1, "mcc": 724, "mnc": 5, "lac": 1234, "cellid": 5678, "rssi": -88, "hod": 88200.0, "hor": "02:15:00", "bat": 12.95, "batb": 4.0, "pb": 85, "tcon": "1", "mot": "a1b2c3d4e5f60708", "efence": 1 } ```
---
Fox  ·  prefix WK  ·  Sigfox asset tracker (no GPS) The GetrakFox has **no GPS receiver**. Location is estimated via Sigfox base station triangulation. Data is delivered via HTTP as JSON from the Sigfox network. It sends two report types indicated by the `rpt` field. ### Report Types | `rpt` | Description | Full telemetry? | |---|---|---| | `"location"` | Network-based position only | No | | `"status"` | Position + device status + sensors | Yes | ### Field Reference | Field | JSON key | Go type | Presence | Description / Notes | |---|---|---|---|---| | Device serial | `mod` | `string` | Always | `WK` + Sigfox device ID (hex) | | Protocol version | `ver` | `int` | Always | Always `1` | | Report type | `rpt` | `string` | Always | `"location"` or `"status"` | | GPS datetime | `dt` | `string` (ISO 8601) | Always | Unix epoch from Sigfox network, UTC | | Server datetime | `dataServidor` | `string` (ISO 8601 ms) | Always | Server receive time, UTC | | GPS fix | `fix` | `uint8` | Always | `1` when estimated radius < 150 m; `0` otherwise | | Latitude | `lat` | `float64` | Always | Estimated latitude (6 decimal places) | | Longitude | `lon` | `float64` | Always | Estimated longitude (6 decimal places) | | Location radius | `rad` | `int` | Always | Geolocation accuracy radius in metres | | Location source | `src` | `int` | Always | `0` = GPS, `1` = WiFi, `2` = Sigfox, etc. | | Location status | `lstt` | `int` | Always | Geolocation compute status code | | Base station | `sfs` | `string` | Always | Sigfox base station ID (hex) | | Sequence number | `seq` | `int` | Always | Sigfox sequence number | | Movement | `mov` | `uint8` | Always | `1` when device is moving | | Sub-event ID | `evs` | `uint8` | Always | Sub-event code from device payload | | External power | `ali` | `uint8` | Always | `1` = external power present | | Ignition | `i` | `int8` | Always | `1` = on · `0` = off · **`-1` = undefined** (on `"location"` reports) | | Digital inputs | `ef` | `uint8` | Always | Input state bitmap | | Thread/channel | `mt` | `uint8` | Always | Always `1` | | Firmware version | `fwv` | `string` | Status only | `MAJOR.MINOR`; omitted when empty | | Device mode | `mode` | `uint8` | Status only | Operating mode code; omitted when `0` | | External battery voltage | `bat` | `float32` | Status only | Main battery (V), raw ÷ 1000; omitted when `0` | | Temperature | `tmp` | `float32` | Status only | Temperature in °C; omitted when `0` | | BLE scan count | `scan` | `uint32` | Status only | BLE advertisements scanned; omitted when `0` | | Communication counter | `com` | `uint32` | Status only | Communication event counter; omitted when `0` | **Fields never emitted:** `velocidade`, `dir`, `ns`, `rt`, `alarmid`, `p`, `s`, `gsms`, `lbs`, `mcc`, `mnc`, `lac`, `cellid`, `hod`, `hor`, `pb`, `batb`, `alt`, `fl`, `mot`, `ev`.
Sample payloads **Location report**: ```json { "mod": "WK1A2B3C4D", "ver": 1, "rpt": "location", "dt": "2026-06-08T14:30:00Z", "dataServidor": "2026-06-08T14:30:00.123Z", "fix": 0, "lat": -23.550652, "lon": -46.633308, "rad": 500, "src": 2, "lstt": 1, "sfs": "1A2B3C", "seq": 42, "mov": 0, "evs": 0, "ali": 1, "i": -1, "ef": 0, "mt": 1 } ``` **Status report**: ```json { "mod": "WK1A2B3C4D", "ver": 1, "rpt": "status", "dt": "2026-06-08T14:31:00Z", "dataServidor": "2026-06-08T14:31:00.456Z", "fix": 1, "lat": -23.550652, "lon": -46.633308, "rad": 120, "src": 2, "lstt": 1, "sfs": "1A2B3C", "seq": 43, "mov": 1, "evs": 0, "ali": 1, "i": 1, "ef": 1, "mt": 1, "fwv": "2.3", "mode": 1, "bat": 3.712, "tmp": 27.0, "scan": 14, "com": 3 } ```
